transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jonas (Redwood CSM), Dana (Blueforge ML Ops), Eliot (Platform), Rina (Security), Marta (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on staging connectivity, credential handoff, and greenlight criteria. Reviewed the access gaps and a short triage of a latency spike from yesterday's dry run. Agreed next steps: send checklist, provision service account, run benchmark, confirm compliance contact.

Topics: staging network, VPC peering / PrivateLink options, KMS/SSO handoff, KV cache warm-up, latency regression troubleshooting, benchmark cadence.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll keep this tight. main agenda is staging greenlight and a quick look at the latency blip from the dry run yesterday.
[00:18] Dana: hi thanks, we have Eli and Rina here too. goal is to get staging fully greenlit by next week so product can start smoke tests.
[00:30] Liam: quick note, we reviewed the logs on our side, the blip was a cold-start + routing fallback to a quantized variant, so you'd see token latency jump.
[00:44] Eliot: yeah that corresponds with our infra logs—there was a transient network route change in the VPC peer. may be flaky BGP flap but not sure.
[01:05] Rina: we also want to confirm KMS keys are tested in staging before any PII touches the pipeline. SOC2 scope folks will ask.
[01:20] Maya: good call. we can provide a checklist for the KMS handshake and SSO (SAML) flow. jonas will follow up with the compliance pack.
[01:34] Jonas: i'll paste the link after the call but broadly we need: service account, short-lived creds, KMS test key ARN, and the audit-logs forwarding route.
[01:50] Marta: one thing—how do we handle KV cache warm-up? the pilot workload has a skewed prefix distribution, so first 10k tokens are heavy.
[02:07] Liam: for that workload i'd recommend a synthetic pre-warm with representative prefixes. our runtime supports prefix caching + auto-eviction tuning. we can share a script.
[02:25] Dana: can that script run inside our utility pod? we don't want outbound traffic from staging to hit prod.
[02:37] Liam: yes, run locally in staging. it will only call the pinned model on your dedicated pool. no prod cross-talk.
[02:49] Eliot: network question: we're leaning toward VPC peering but curious about PrivateLink. which has fewer route flaps?
[03:01] Liam: PrivateLink is generally more stable for cross-account connectivity since it avoids route tables; peering is fine but needs careful route management. PrivateLink adds a small egress cost but reduces noisy neighbor exposure.
[03:20] Rina: cost is fine if it reduces audit surface. the security team prefers PrivateLink + enforced RBAC and VPC endpoints.
[03:33] Maya: noted. next step: we'll include both patterns in the access doc so you can pick.
[03:40] Dana: on the latency blip, can you share the token-level breakdown? the dry-run trace had some missing timestamps in our logs.
[03:52] Liam: sure, i'll attach the per-token trace and a CSV with token times, but quick takeaway: 70% of requests hit the cache but the failing trace had a cache miss, then a model fallback - quantized 8-bit variant that increased kernel launch time.
[04:15] Eliot: is fallback automatic? we would prefer to keep consistent variant to avoid jitter.
[04:25] Liam: default policy will fall back to compatible variant when capacity is constrained. you can set strict routing to avoid fallback and instead queue or fail fast. it's a tradeoff: availability vs latency predictability.
[04:44] Dana: we want predictability for product tests. can we set routing to strict for staging?
[04:51] Maya: yes, staging can use strict routing. for prod maybe a more lenient policy. we'll include config snippets.
[05:01] Marta: also curious about observability retention—how long are token-level traces kept in staging vs prod?
[05:10] Jonas: by default 7 days for token traces in staging; we can bump that for the pilot if needed but it's an add-on cost.
[05:22] Rina: SOC2 folks will ask about audit log export to our SIEM—does Redwood support log push?
[05:30] Liam: yes, we support pushing audit logs to your S3/Cloud Storage or streaming to your SIEM; we also have prebuilt connectors for Splunk and Datadog.
[05:41] Eliot: ok good. about credentials: we'll make a service account but need the exact IAM roles.
[05:49] Maya: we'll include a minimal IAM role set in the checklist. it's basically call-only access to the inference endpoint + KMS decrypt for test key + write-only to audit-s3.
[06:02] Dana: timeline check: if we get the checklist today and create the service account by Friday, when can we run a benchmark?
[06:11] Liam: we can run a benchmark as early as next Tuesday; need the service account and KMS in place. i'll prepare the harness and sample prompt set.
[06:20] Maya: agreed. also we'll run small A/B with strict routing vs fallback to show latency distributions.
[06:28] Marta: excellent. one hiccup from product—the UI team saw tokenization mismatches between your runtime and our tokenizer for a few prompt templates.
[06:40] Liam: that's usually due to newline normalization or special unicode normalization. we can run a tokenizer diff tool; i'll drop the script.
[06:50] Eliot: great, that should be quick.
[06:56] Rina: about the KMS test key, do you need a symmetric or asymmetric key?
[07:02] Liam: symmetric is fine for envelope encryption and the decrypt calls we use. asymmetric is only needed for special signing flows.
[07:12] Maya: recap: we'll send checklist + network diagrams, share IAM snippets, and Liam will prep the benchmark harness.
[07:23] Dana: can you also include a short runbook for failover? yesterday we improvised and want a rehearsed path.
[07:30] Jonas: i'll include a 1-page failover runbook: rollback to pinned variant, disable fallback, and how to scale the pool.
[07:40] Eliot: small question about region placement—we have users in EU, we'd like staging to be in us-west for now, but product would like to test eu-west later. can we move models between regions in the pilot?
[07:55] Liam: yes, model variants can be deployed per-region; moving takes a model artifact copy and a cold-start window. we can simulate cross-region latency in the benchmark.
[08:08] Marta: that will help.
[08:12] Dana: any competitors or other tech we should be aware of? we briefly evaluated Anthropic's embedder but your cost/perf looks better for our use case.
[08:22] Maya: thanks. we also shared a short cost projection—we'll update it after the benchmark.
[08:30] Rina: compliance: i'll send our SOC2 contact and the specific questions about key rotation and key custody.
[08:39] Rina: one more, do you provide customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key)?
[08:44] Liam: yes, BYOK for Private deployment and VPC flows; for hosted we support envelope encryption with your KMS. we'll document the options.
[08:55] Dana: perfect. any blockers on your side?
[09:00] Maya: nothing major. we'll share the docs today.
[09:04] Jonas: action items we'll sync in CRM and i'll attach the compliance pack and the network diagram.
[09:12] Eliot: quick nit—can we get the benchmark harness to output p50/p95/p99 and a per-token breakdown?
[09:20] Liam: yep default output includes p50/p90/p95/p99 and per-token CSV.
[09:26] Marta: timing: can we run an initial small pass before the big benchmark to validate credentials? maybe a 30-min smoke test?
[09:35] Liam: absolutely yes. small smoke test once creds are set, then full benchmark on Tuesday.
[09:41] Dana: ok that sets expectations.
[09:44] Maya: final recap of next steps—send checklist and diagrams (Maya), provision service account (Blueforge / Eliot), KMS test key (Blueforge / Eliot), benchmark harness prep (Liam), compliance contact (Rina). we'll reconvene after the smoke test results.
[09:59] Maya: thanks all, i'll send the deck and links. any last Qs?
[10:04] Marta: none. thanks.
[10:06] meeting end

Post-call notes (auto):
- Maya uploaded a short staging checklist link (placeholder) to CRM.
- Liam to attach per-token trace from yesterday's dry run and the tokenizer diff script.
- Blueforge to confirm KMS and service account by Friday to enable Tuesday benchmark.
